sanskrit: tad id āsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ yato jajña ugras tveṣanṛmṇaḥ | sadyo jajñāno ni riṇāti śatrūn anu yaṃ viśve madanty ūmāḥ ||
english: That was the foremost among the worlds from which was born the Fierce One, blazing with virile might; born forthwith, he shatters enemies; all the helpers exult after him.

sanskrit: vāvṛdhānaḥ śavasā bhūryojāḥ śatrur dāsāya bhiyasaṃ dadhāti | avyanac ca vyanac ca sasni saṃ te navanta prabhṛtā madeṣu ||
english: Swelling with power, abounding in strength, he places fear in the slave-foe; both the unclad and the clad bow down to thee, the champion, at the gift-offerings in the festal joys.

sanskrit: tve kratum api pṛñcanti viśve dvir yad ete trir bhavanty ūmāḥ | svādoḥ svādīyaḥ svādunā sṛjā sam adaḥ su madhu madhunābhi yodhīḥ ||
english: All helpers mix their will in thee when these come twice and thrice together. Sweeter than the sweet, blend that sweet one together; truly that honey — do thou cleave to it with honey.

sanskrit: iti cid dhi tvā dhanā jayantaṃ raṇeraṇe anumadanti viprāḥ | ojīyo dhṛṣṇo sthiram ā tanuṣva mā tvā dabhan durevā yātudhānāḥ ||
english: For thus, as the winner of riches, the sages extol thee in battle after battle. More mighty, O Bold One, extend thyself firmly; may the ill-intentioned sorcerers not deceive thee.

sanskrit: tvayā vayaṃ śāśadmahe raṇeṣu prapaśyanto yudhenyāni bhūri | codayāmi ta āyudhā vacobhiḥ saṃ te śyāmi brahmaṇā vayāṃsi ||
english: Through thee we have prevailed in battles, beholding many things worthy of war. With my words I urge thy weapons forward; with sacred speech I strengthen thy pinions.

sanskrit: stuṣeyyaṃ puruvarpasam ṛbhvam inatamam āptyam āptyānām | ā darśate śavasā sapta dānūn pra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri ||
english: May I praise him of many forms, the Skilled One, the mightiest, the child of the Āptyas, lord among the Āptyas; with his strength he makes the seven rivers appear, overcoming multitudes of counterparts.

sanskrit: ni tad dadhiṣe 'varaṃ paraṃ ca yasminn āvithāvasā duroṇe | ā mātarā sthāpayase jigatnū ata inoṣi karvarā purūṇi ||
english: Thou dost establish both the nearer and the farther, him in whose dwelling thou hast protected with thy help; thou dost make the two swift-moving Mothers stand firm, and from there thou accomplishest manifold deeds.

sanskrit: imā brahma bṛhaddivo vivakti- -indrāya śūṣam agriyaḥ svarṣāḥ | maho gotrasya kṣayati svarājo duraś ca viśvā avṛṇod apa svāḥ ||
english: These prayers Bṛhaddiva, the foremost, the sun-seeker, proclaims as might for Indra; the self-sovereign dwells in the great enclosure and has opened wide all his own doors.

sanskrit: evā mahān bṛhaddivo atharvā- -avocat svāṃ tanvam indram eva | svasāro mātaribhvarīr ariprā hinvanti ca śavasā vardhayanti ca ||
english: Thus did Bṛhaddiva Atharvan, the great one, declare Indra himself to be his own body; the sisterly winds of Mātariśvan, stainless, both urge him on and increase him with strength.

sanskrit: ṛdhaṅmandrayoninovibhāvā amṛtāsuḥ sujanmā vardhamānaḥ | adabdhāsur bhrājamāno 'heva trito dādhāra trīṇi ||
english: Prospering, of exhilarating origin, radiant in manifestation, with immortal breath, nobly born, growing; with breath undeceived, shining — like a serpent Trita has upheld the three.

sanskrit: ni yo dharmaṇi prathamaḥ sasāda- -ato vapūṃṣi kṛṇute purūṇi | dhāsyur yoniṃ prathama ā viveśa- -ā yo vācam anuditāṃ cikāya ||
english: He who first settled in the ordinance — from thence he fashions manifold forms; the nourishing one first entered the womb, he who has heeded the unuttered word.

sanskrit: yas te śokas tanva ārireca kṣarad dhiraṇyaṃ śucayo 'nu svāḥ | atrā dadhiṣe amṛtāni nāma- -asme vastrāṇīṣa erayanta ||
english: He whose heat poured forth from thy body, dripping gold, pure, following their own nature — here thou dost hold the immortal names; the robes, O master, are set in motion for us.

sanskrit: pra yad ete prataraṃ pūrvyaṃ guḥ sadaḥsada ātiṣṭhanto ajuryam | kaviḥ śuṣasya mātarā rihāṇe jāmirvadhuryuḥpratimānimīta ||
english: When these have proclaimed the ancient foremost thing, standing seat by seat on that which ages not — the Sage, as the two Mothers of vitality lick him, has measured the kinsman-bride's form as counterpart.

sanskrit: tad ū ṣu te mahā pṛthuryaman namaḥ kaviḥ kāvyenākṛṇot | yat samyañco 'bhiyanto *'dhi kṣām adhā mahī rodhacakrā vavardha ||
english: That great and broad ruling power — the Sage has fashioned it with his wisdom, O Yama, in reverence; when the converging ones press toward the earth, then the great wheel of obstruction has grown.

sanskrit: sapta maryādāḥ kavayas tatakṣus tāsām id ekām abhy aṃhuro gāt | utāmṛtāsur vṛta eṣi kṛṇvann asura āptaḥ svadhayā samadguḥ ||
english: The seven sages have fashioned the seven bounds; towards one of them the sinful one has gone; yet thou who art immortal in breath, encompassed, advancing, O Asura, attained, goest along by thine own power.

sanskrit: utāyur jyeṣṭho ratnā dadhāty ūrjā vā yaṃ sacate kavir dāḥ | putro vā yat pitarā kṣatram īrte jyeṣṭhaṃ maryādam ahvayan svasti ||
english: The eldest life sets down its treasures, or the Sage, the giver, is attended by vigour; or when a son urges the kingly power against his parents, calling the eldest bound with blessing.

sanskrit: darśan nu tān varuṇa ye ta iṣṭāv āvarvṛtataḥ kṛṇavo vapūṃṣi | ardham ardhena śavasā pṛṇakṣy ardhena śuṣmaṃ vardhase *'mūra ||
english: Look now upon those, O Varuṇa, who have turned back again at thy sacrifice; thou dost fashion forms — thou fillest one half with the other's power, and with half thou increasest thy vigour, O Unwildering.

sanskrit: avīvṛdhāma śagmyaṃ sakhāyaṃ varuṇaṃ putram aditer iṣiram | kaviśastāny asmai vacāṃsy avocāma rodasī satyavācau ||
english: We have magnified the powerful friend, Varuṇa the vigorous son of Aditi; we have spoken for him the words proclaimed by the Sage, to the two Worlds truthful in speech.

sanskrit: ko vaḥ paścāt prāvicchāyat kaḥ puraḥ prākhanat pathaḥ | yadaita tvaramāṇā varuṇaprasūtā āpaḥ ||
english: Who drove you forth from behind? Who dug out the paths in front, when you, the Waters urged on by Varuṇa, came hurrying?

sanskrit: prajāpatir asṛjata sa puraḥ prākhanat pathaḥ | sa u no anv avāsṛjat tena sṛṣṭāḥ kṣarāmasi ||
english: Prajāpati released you; he dug out the paths in front; and he in turn released us from behind — released by him, we flow.

sanskrit: punānā āpo bahudhā sravanti- -imāṃś ca lokān pradiśaś ca sarvāḥ | punantv asmān duritād avadyān muñcantu mṛtyor nirṛter upasthāt ||
english: The purifying Waters flow in many ways, through all these worlds and through all the regions; may they purify us from sin and blame; may they release us from the lap of death and dissolution.

sanskrit: āpo asmān mātaraḥ sūdayantu ghṛtena no ghṛtapuvaḥ punantu | viśvaṃ hi ripraṃ pravahanti devīr ud id ābhyaḥ śucir ā pūta emi ||
english: May the Waters, our mothers, refine us; may the clarified-butter purifiers purify us with ghee; for the divine ones carry away all defilement — from them indeed I come forth pure, cleansed.

sanskrit: āpo devīr mātaraḥ sūdayiṣṇavo ghṛtaścuto madhunā saṃ papṛcre | tā asmabhyaṃ sūrayo viśvam āyuḥ kṣapa usrā varivasyantu śubhrāḥ ||
english: The divine Waters, our mothers, intent on refining, dripping with ghee, have mingled together with honey; may those bright ones, the divine ones, bestow on us the whole span of life by night and by day.

sanskrit: udakasyodakatamā revattamā revatīnām | śundhantām āpaḥ śundhantv asmān ||
english: Most watery of waters, most wealthy of the wealthy ones — may the Waters purify; may they purify us.

sanskrit: yūyam āpo vīraśriyo yūyaṃ sūdayathā śucīn | yuṣmākam id diśo mahīr īyante pradiśaḥ pṛthak ||
english: You, O Waters, hold the glory of heroes; you refine the pure ones; your great directions, the sub-regions separate, flow in motion.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya yonir yūyaṃ somasya dhenavo madhiṣṭhāḥ | yuṣmān devīr deva ā kṣiyatīndur yūyaṃ jinvata brahmakṣatram āpaḥ ||
english: You are the womb of Mitra and Varuṇa; you are the sweetest milk-cows of Soma; the god Indu takes up his dwelling in you, O divine ones; O Waters, gladden the brahman power and the kṣatra power.

sanskrit: śaśvad ābhiḥ śāśadānāḥ śamanānvayāmasi | āpo viśvasya sūdanīr yā devā manave dadhuḥ ||
english: Continually prevailing through these, we go pursuing the appeasers; the Waters are the refiners of all — those which the gods gave to Manu.

sanskrit: yad dhāvanti punate tad āpo yat tiṣṭhanti śuddhā it tad bhavanti | nāsām avadyam avidaṃ na ripraṃ sanād eva madhunā saṃ papṛcre ||
english: When they flow, the Waters purify; when they stand still, they become purely clean; I have found no blame in them, no defilement — from of old they have been mingled together with honey.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ pra cakramur hitvāvadyam āpaḥ | śataṃ ca vaḥ prasravaṇeṣu devīḥ sahasraṃ ca pavitāraḥ punanti ||
english: Golden-hued, pure, purifying, the Waters have strode forward, having cast away blame; a hundred of you, O divine ones, and a thousand purifying filters purify at the outpourings.

sanskrit: tās tādṛśīr brahmāṇaṃ sūdayanty aṅgoṣṭhyā stotryā jīvadhanyāḥ | yā viśvasya śucikṛto ayātor gāva iva payasā sthā sujātāḥ ||
english: Such as they are, life-bestowing, they refine the brahman whose toes they touch, worthy of praise; those who make everything pure, who do not pass away — like cows, well-born, you stand with milk.

sanskrit: viśvād riprān muñcata sindhavo no yāny enāṃsi cakṛmā tanūbhiḥ | indrapraśiṣṭā varuṇaprasūtā ā siñcatāpo madhv ā samudre ||
english: Release us from all defilements, O rivers, from whatever sins we have committed with our bodies; directed by Indra, urged on by Varuṇa, pour in honey, O Waters, into the ocean.
